observations: Bare engine block pulled from a vehicle, sitting on a stand/table, no transmission bell housing visible attached in a car.
Wiring harness, belts, pulleys, alternator, and intake manifold are present and appear intact.
Orange and purple paint dabs on the cylinder head, likely yard/inventory marking, not a manufacturer code.
A security/anti-theft strap is wrapped around the engine, consistent with yard storage.
Watermark reads 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' - this is the seller's shop name/watermark, not a model plate for the engine itself.
No engine code, VIN tag, or manufacturer plate is legible in any of the three photos.
Background shows a rough concrete-floor workshop/yard, consistent with a used spare-parts dealer.

identity.kind: used car engine (pulled/salvage engine, make and model not legible)

claims.claim: We all so deals on in all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: General business claim, not about this specific engine's condition or fitment; nothing in photos confirms or denies it.

risks.risk: Engine make, model, and displacement are unknown, so correct vehicle fitment and price bracket cannot be determined.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code/casting number stamp (usually on block near bell housing) or a VIN/engine tag.
risks.if_unproven: Cannot be priced at all, since engine value varies enormously by make/model/displacement.

risks.risk: Unknown whether the engine runs or starts; internal condition (compression, bearings, timing components) cannot be seen.
risks.proof: A video of the engine being started and idling, plus a compression test reading.

risks.risk: Mileage and history (accident, flood, overheating) are not verifiable from static photos.
risks.proof: Odometer photo from the donor vehicle or paperwork showing mileage/history.

risks.risk: Completeness cannot be confirmed; some sensors, brackets, or the turbo/intake parts may be missing or swapped.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set including the back of the block, oil pan, and both sides of the cylinder head.
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming missing ancillary parts (incomplete engine).

risks.risk: Visible oil residue/staining could indicate leaks or past overhaul rather than just handling grease.
risks.proof: Close-up of oil pan gasket and rear main seal area, dry and clean, after wiping.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the engine code/casting number stamped on the block.
Confirmation from seller of the exact make, model, and year range this engine fits.
Video of the engine starting and running, or at minimum turning over.
Additional photos of the back of the block, oil pan, and underside to confirm completeness.
Any paperwork or tag indicating origin (import tag, mileage, auction sheet).
response.reason: The photos show an engine but no legible code, make, or model, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without knowing what vehicle it fits; the seller's general claim about dealing in spare parts says nothing about this specific unit's identity or condition.
